gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watts each kit's own panel can supply around the clock in November sun. With the US November average of 3.53 sun-hours and a 75% panel derate, that is about 22 W for every 200 W-panel kit, 44 W for the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 400 W, and 66 W for the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 600 W kit ($798 on ALLPOWERS' US store today). The 600 W kit's panel refills the 1,024 Wh battery in about 0.64 of a November day, against roughly 2 days for the 200 W kits.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts' same-panel-watts article (updated 2026-11-12), Lights On Labs (2026-10-27), PowerSized's kit price guide (checked through 2026-11-14) and Prepared States (2026-11-06/07). All four already publish cost per Wh and refill hours. Those refill hours are either 'full sun' (Wh ÷ panel W) or a generic derate (StormWatts uses ×0.85 at 4.5 sun-hours, PowerSized ×0.75). None turns the panel into watts it can sustain around the clock in an actual outage month. None lists the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 600 W kit. Prepared States shows only the P1800 + 200 W kit, at $538.99.
decides: For a multi-day outage, the useful limit is the panel's daily harvest, not the battery. Every 200 W kit (BLUETTI AC180, Elite 100 V2, Jackery 1000 v2, ALLPOWERS P1800 + 200 W) refills about 22 W around the clock in November, roughly one Wi-Fi router plus a few LED bulbs. That makes battery size (AC180 1,152 Wh vs 1,024 Wh) a minor difference. The ALLPOWERS P1800 + 600 W kit at $798 sustains about 3× that (66 W) for $12 per sustained watt, against about $35 for the AC180 kit. It should be the solar-backup pick under $1,000, as long as its panel layout and ship date check out. The P1800 + 400 W at $698 is the cheaper step-down (44 W). The DELTA 3 Classic kit at $669 is a short-outage, wall-recharge pick, because if its panel is 160 W (as PowerSized lists) it refills only about 18 W.
